local_market_longform:
Reno is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in Reno currently trade around a median of $560,000 and take roughly 38 days to go under contract, with about 24% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. Reno runs heavily to early-1900s cottages in the older core and heavy 1990s–2010s tract and master-planned growth south and north, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around Reno, the issues we see most are high-desert freeze-thaw cracking, wildfire exposure in the foothills, seismic risk on regional faults, and aging swamp coolers. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like Midtown out to Sparks and Carson City — and in Nevada the local economy anchored by Tesla's Gigafactory and the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center, logistics, and California out-migration keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Washoe County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the Reno sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near the Reno Arch also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen Reno. We know what a block in Midtown, the Wells Avenue district, Northwest Reno, and Sun Valley actually sells for, what the Truckee Meadows buyers will and won't pay for, and how Washoe County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

situations.body: Settling an estate — often from out of state — is hard enough without a listing on top of it. We buy inherited Reno homes as-is, work alongside the Washoe County probate process, and let you take what matters and leave the rest.

situations.title: The house needs too much work
situations.body: Fire, water, foundation, or years of deferred repairs — we've bought all of it around Reno. No cleaning, no contractors, no staging.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my Reno house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Nevada title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in Reno pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy Reno homes in any condition — including the high-desert freeze-thaw cracking we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your Reno neighborhood — places like Midtown — the home's condition, and current the Truckee Meadows demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Nevada?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Nevada permits direct purchases when acting on your own behalf; we buy as a principal, not as your agent.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Washoe County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
